title: Satay Ayam
subtitle: indonesian and malaysian chicken satay
excerpt: Satay ayam is marinated chicken threaded onto skewers and grilled until charred and smoky, then served with a rich peanut dipping sauce. The marinade uses turmeric, lemongrass, and coriander. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Satay is one of the most recognisable dishes in Southeast Asian cooking, popular across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. Ayam means chicken in both Indonesian and Malay.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken can marinate overnight in the fridge. The peanut sauce keeps for 3 days refrigerated.

glossaryTerms.definition: Skewered marinated meat grilled over charcoal or a hot grill. A street food staple across Southeast Asia.
A dipping sauce made from ground peanuts, coconut milk, chilli, and lime. Served alongside satay and gado-gado across the region.

content.text: ayam takes most of its flavour from the marinade and the char from the grill. The chicken needs at least an hour to marinate, but overnight is better. Serves 4.
should be made ahead of time. It thickens as it cools; thin with a little warm water before serving.
Mix the lemongrass, turmeric, coriander, cumin, sugar, and oil together. Toss with the chicken cubes. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Make the peanut sauce. Blend the peanuts, coconut milk, chilli, lime juice, and soy sauce until smooth. Add water to reach a dipping consistency. Taste and adjust.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes. Thread 4 to 5 chicken pieces onto each skewer.
Heat a griddle pan over high heat until very hot. Cook the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Rest the skewers for 2 minutes before serving with the peanut sauce alongside.

attrs.problem: The chicken is burning on the outside but raw inside.
attrs.solution: Cut the chicken into smaller, even pieces. If using very hot charcoal, move skewers to a cooler part of the grill after the initial sear.

attrs.problem: The peanut sauce is too thick.
attrs.solution: Add warm water a tablespoon at a time and stir between additions. The sauce thickens as it cools so make it a little looser than you think you need.
The pan was not hot enough. Get the griddle smoking before laying the skewers down. Do not move them for the first 3 minutes.

content.text: Satay is eaten across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. It is sold from street carts over charcoal grills. The Indonesian and Malaysian versions use the spiced turmeric marinade that gives the chicken its yellow colour. Served with peanut sauce and compressed rice, it is one of the defining street foods of the region.
